newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: HOCKEY-NZ beat Belgium in hockey World Cup pool.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-NZ beat Belgium in hockey World Cup pool.

text.p: WELLINGTON, March 11 - New Zealand bounced back from conceding an early goal to beat Belgium 3-1 in a critical pool match at the hockey World Cup qualifying tournament in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday (NZT), NZPA reports.

Canterbury forward John Radovonich scored three goals in five minutes late in the second half to set up the Kiwis' victory after they had let in a second-minute goal and then completely dominated the match without being able to find the net.

The result keeps alive New Zealand's chances of making the semi-finals, although they must still rely on unbeaten pool leaders South Korea at least drawing with Argentina on Tuesday for that to happen.
If New Zealand qualify second in their pool -- the highest they can finish -- they will almost certainly meet Atlanta Olympics silver medallists Spain in the semi-finals.
Should they only finish third in their pool, they will go into a sudden-death match for a place in May's 12-team World Cup in the Netherlands.
New Zealand played strongly, controlling the pace of the game, but their relentless attacking had gone unrewarded at halftime when they still trailed 0-1.
The attacks continued in the second spell, with the Kiwis forcing six unsuccessful penalty corners and continuing to shoot wide or making loose passes when chances beckoned.

However, as the Belgians wilted in the heat, which reached 40 deg C during the match, 32-year-old Radovonich, who has won over 50 caps for New Zealand, bounced for field goals in the 62nd, 65th and 67th minutes.
New Zealand forced several more chances in the final eight minutes to thoroughly deserve their win.

Apart from Radovonich, others to impress were captain Jamie Smith, whose phenomenal work rate was a feature of the match, Andrew van der Bent, Umesh Parag and Darren Smith, who made incisive dribbles through the Belgian defence.
New Zealand now have two days' rest before playoffs begin on Thursday.
